paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: being familiar with Jesus is not the same as believing in Him. The hometown crowd could name His mother, His brothers and His sisters. They knew Him as the carpenter's son, and they "took offense at Him" (Matthew 13:57). They kept asking where He got His wisdom and miraculous powers (Matthew 13:54-56).

Look at what Jesus says: "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). Then comes the heavy part. "He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). I think that one stings, because the people closest to Him had a front-row seat and still took offense.

So ask yourself, baker: have I gotten so used to the Bible that I stopped being amazed by it? You can know the stories, the verses and the songs by heart, and still shrug. So bring your belief with you when you open the Word, and let Jesus surprise you like He did that day in the synagogue (Matthew 13:54). I've been tucked away in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you, being amazed again is a gift.
